question: A 45-year-old woman with diabetic peripheral neuropathy reports burning pain and electric-shock sensations in both feet, inadequately controlled on regular paracetamol. Which adjuvant analgesic class has the strongest evidence base for this neuropathic pain?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: NSAIDs target prostaglandin-mediated nociception (peripheral inflammation). They have minimal efficacy in neuropathic pain, which arises from ectopic neuronal discharge rather than inflammatory mediators.

Correct. Gabapentinoids block voltage-gated calcium channels (α2δ subunit), reducing ectopic neuronal discharge in sensitised afferents. Pregabalin and gabapentin are first-line adjuvants for diabetic neuropathy, post-herpetic neuralgia, and central neuropathic pain.
Opioids have some efficacy in neuropathic pain but are not first-line due to tolerance, dependence risk, and side-effect burden. Gabapentinoids and SNRIs/TCAs are preferred first steps.
Baclofen (GABAB agonist) is used for spasticity and trigeminal neuralgia. It is not the primary adjuvant for peripheral diabetic neuropathy.

overallFeedback.feedback: For neuropathic pain (burning, shooting, electric-shock quality), first-line adjuvants are gabapentinoids (pregabalin/gabapentin) and SNRIs/TCAs — not NSAIDs or routine opioids.
Correct. Gabapentinoids (pregabalin, gabapentin) are first-line adjuvant analgesics for neuropathic pain by targeting the α2δ calcium channel subunit.
